subject: general
question: Sapna invested ₹21,200 on simple interest, partly at the rate of 13% per annum and partly at the rate of 3% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 8 years, then find the sum invested at the rate of 13% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When Simple Interests from two investments are equal for the same duration, the ratio of the principals is inversely proportional to their respective interest rates.

Ratio of investments = P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁ = 3 : 13

Total units of investment = 3 + 13 = 16 units

Sum invested at 13% (P₁) = (3 ÷ 16) × 21200

P₁ = 3 × 1325 = ₹3,975

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,975.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 Total Sum: ₹21,200
